newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major bids to win over voters with mail-shot.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major bids to win over voters with mail-shot.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major, who insists he will not call a general election until next year, said on Sunday he was writing to more than two million voters in key districts to convince them his policies were right.

With the ruling Conservatives trailing the opposition Labour Party by up to 30 points in opinion polls, Major has already raised the pre-election temperature with a tour around the country and a new poster campaign.

Major, who surprised pundits with his 1992 election victory, is now down to a one-seat overall majority in the 651-seat parliament. But he said last week: "I am not going to call an election this year. The election will be next year."
He has to call one by May 1997 at the latest.
On Sunday, in an article for the tabloid News of the World, he revealed Conservative plans for an unprecedented mail-shot to voters in 104 key constituencies where the next election could be decided.
"I know our decision to raise taxes during the worldwide recession was unwelcome. I regret the fact that we had to do it but it was the right thing to do," he wrote.
"Today the IMF (International Monetary Fund) describes our economy as enviable. That's why we say - Yes it hurt, Yes it worked," he added,
Major was given predictably short shrift by Labour, riding high in the polls under its centrist leader Tony Blair despite rumbling discontent from some supporters who see his style as dictatorial.
Finance spokesman Gordon Brown said: "Whatever he says in a letter, the people will never forget that the Tories (Conservatives) lied about tax at the last election and they're lying about tax now."
Not to be outdone, Labour has retorted with its own six-poster campaign, launched at the weekend by Blair.
With inflation low, unemployment falling and house prices rising, the Conservatives hope the return of the much-touted "feelgood factor" will salvage their electoral fortunes.
But polling experts fear time is running out for Major.

"The Tories are gradually eroding Labour's lead in the Gallup poll but the process is so far proving glacial," noted expert Professor Anthony King wrote after the latest opinion poll. "It will take an avalanche for them to win next time."
